cases.name: move-one-forward
cases.covers: One page moved to the end. The destination is a position in the POST-REMOVAL index space, which is the only frame where the answer is unambiguous.

cases.name: move-one-backward
cases.covers: And the other way, to the front.

cases.name: move-block-preserves-caller-order
cases.covers: Two pages named in an order that is not their document order. They land as one contiguous block in the order GIVEN, not in the order they were in.

cases.name: move-to-same-place
cases.covers: A move that changes nothing, which is a move rather than a refusal.

cases.name: move-duplicate-refused
cases.covers: The same page twice. Deduplicating would silently change what the caller asked for, and the destination would be ambiguous.

cases.name: move-nothing-refused
cases.covers: An empty list, which names no pages to move and no move to make.

cases.name: rotate-nothing-refused
cases.covers: The same on the other two operations.

cases.name: delete-nothing-refused
cases.covers: And on the delete.

cases.name: move-unknown-page-refused
cases.covers: An object number no page has.

cases.name: rotate-one
cases.covers: A page rotated to an angle it did not have.

cases.name: rotate-to-zero
cases.covers: Back to upright, which is a rotation rather than a removal: /Rotate 0 is a value the page carries.

cases.name: rotate-several
cases.covers: Several pages to one angle, which flattens four different rotations into one.

cases.name: rotate-unknown-page-refused
cases.covers: A list naming one page that does not exist. Nothing is rotated: the whole list resolves before anything is written.

cases.name: insert-blank-at-end
cases.covers: A blank page appended, which is what an absent destination means. Its object number is fresh and is resolved from the list AFTER the insert: it does not exist before.

cases.name: insert-blank-at-front
cases.covers: Three blank pages at the front, which pushes every existing page down by three.

cases.name: insert-blank-in-the-middle
cases.covers: And in the middle, where the new pages land contiguously.

cases.name: insert-blank-bad-size-refused
cases.covers: A page with no area is not a page.

cases.name: insert-blank-too-many-refused
cases.covers: Past the batch ceiling. A larger batch is a loop at the call site; the number is shared with the server so a client never finds a lower one by surprise.

cases.name: insert-document
cases.covers: Every page of another PDF, deep-copied in. The copy is not a full detach: an imported stream still reads through the source, so the source has to outlive every future save.

cases.name: insert-document-at-end
cases.covers: The same with no destination, which appends.

cases.name: flatten-annotated-page
cases.covers: A page with annotations turned into content. Irreversible, and it is the page that changes rather than the page list.

cases.name: flatten-for-print
cases.covers: The other usage. An annotation may carry a different stream for each, and a stamp hidden on screen that prints is what makes the distinction matter.

cases.name: flatten-page-with-nothing-on-it
cases.covers: A page with no annotations, which is UNCHANGED rather than failed: a page with nothing to flatten is already flat.

cases.name: flatten-duplicate-refused
cases.covers: The same page twice. The second would flatten what the first already did.

cases.name: delete-one
cases.covers: A page removed. Its object number is RETIRED rather than freed, so per-page state a caller kept can never attach to an unrelated future page.

cases.name: delete-several
cases.covers: Several at once, which leaves the survivors in their original relative order.

cases.name: delete-every-page-refused
cases.covers: A document with no pages is not a document.

cases.name: delete-unknown-page-refused
cases.covers: An object number no page has. Nothing is deleted.
